steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a high-level, conceptual run-through of how a Transformer works:

1. Input Representation  
   • Each token (word or subword) is converted into a continuous vector (an embedding).  
   • A positional encoding is added so the model knows the order of tokens (since attention itself is order-agnostic).

2. Self-Attention Mechanism  
   • For each token, three vectors are computed by linear projections of its embedding: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V).  
   • Attention scores between token i and token j are computed as the dot product of Qi and Kj (scaled and soft-maxed).  
   • Each token’s new representation is a weighted sum of all token Vs, where the weights come from those attention scores—so every token “looks at” all others in the sequence.

3. Multi-Head Attention  
   • Instead of doing one single attention, the model runs several in parallel (“heads”) with different learned projections.  
   • This lets it capture different types of relationships (e.g. syntax in one head, semantics in another).  
   • Outputs of all heads are concatenated and linearly transformed back to the model dimension.

4. Feed-Forward Network  
   • After attention, each token’s vector goes through the same small two-layer neural network (position-wise).  
   • Typically it’s a ReLU or GELU layer sandwiched between two linear layers.

5. Residual Connections & Layer Normalization  
   • Each sub-layer (attention or feed-forward) has a “skip connection” adding its input to its output.  
   • Layer normalization is applied to stabilize and speed up training.

6. Stacking Layers  
   • You repeat the attention + feed-forward blocks N times (e.g. 6, 12, 24 layers) so the model can build up increasingly abstract representations.

7. Encoder vs. Decoder (for sequence-to-sequence tasks)  
   • Encoder: stacks only self-attention and feed-forward.  
   • Decoder: has masked self-attention (to prevent peeking at future tokens) plus encoder-decoder attention (so the output can attend to input representations).

8. Final Output  
   • In language modeling or translation, the decoder’s top layer outputs a vector per position.  
   • A final linear layer + softmax turns that into a probability distribution over the vocabulary.

Key Intuition  
• Self-attention lets every position flexibly weigh every other position, capturing long-range dependencies in parallel (unlike RNNs).  
• Multi-head attention broadens the model’s perspective.  
• Residuals and normalization make deep stacks trainable.
